sources.note: FMA paper: genre labels are hierarchical/noisy; audio features and train/validation/test splits are important.
Techno: 120-150 BPM, 4/4, repetitive, electronic instruments, rhythm-oriented.
House: repetitive four-on-the-floor, 115-130 BPM, off-beat hats, drum machines, basslines, vocals optional.
Drum and bass: fast breakbeats around 165-185 BPM with heavy bass/sub-bass.
Dubstep: syncopated/shuffled 132-142 BPM rhythms, strong sub-bass and sparse half-time feel.
Ambient: tone/atmosphere over traditional rhythm, sustained textures, low beat density.
City pop: loose Japanese urban pop label drawing on funk, disco, R&B, AOR, soft rock, boogie, jazz fusion and synth production.
Punk rock: stripped-down guitars/bass/drums/vocals, fast tempos, distorted power chords, less syncopation.
Heavy metal: loud distorted guitars, emphatic rhythms, dense bass/drums, vigorous vocals and riffs.
Funk: syncopated groove, prominent bassline, emphasis on the first beat, danceable interlocking rhythms.
Hip-hop: rapping over beats, sampling, loops, turntablism and drum-machine/sampler production.
Trance: 120-150 BPM, repeated melodic phrases, long builds and peaks/drops.

アンビエント.notes: atmosphere, low beat density, sustained tone

ドローン.notes: sustained or slowly changing tones, very low onset density

ノイズミュージック.notes: noise texture, high zero-crossing/high-frequency energy, unstable tonality

電子音楽.notes: broad electronic macro label; synth/drum-machine production

テクノ.notes: 120-150 BPM, repetitive 4/4, rhythm over melody, synthetic timbre

ディープ・ハウス.notes: house grid with warmer/deeper bass and smoother energy

トランス.notes: 120-150 BPM, repeated melodic phrases and build-ups

チップチューン.notes: simple waveform/square-wave timbre, high ZCR, synthetic melody

ヒップホップ.notes: beats/loops, rap vocal presence, sampling, low-mid body

トラップ.notes: 808/sub-bass, sparse high hats, half/double-time tempo ambiguity

レゲエ.notes: offbeat skank, strong bass, slower groove

ダブ.notes: reggae-derived bass, sparse arrangement, echo/reverb space

ファンク.notes: syncopated bass/guitar groove, prominent low end, danceable interlocking rhythms

ソウルミュージック.notes: lead vocal focus, groove, warm midrange

ディスコ.notes: dance pop/funk with four-on-the-floor, bright rhythmic production

パンク.notes: fast stripped-down distorted guitars, dry heavy drums, low complexity

メタル.notes: distorted guitars, riffs, emphatic rhythms, dense low/mid energy

ジャズ.notes: acoustic or electric ensemble, swing/syncopation, harmonic/chroma complexity

シティ・ポップ.notes: Japanese urban pop vibe, funk/disco/R&B/AOR/soft rock/boogie/jazz fusion/synth production

J-POP.notes: vocal-led Japanese pop, chorus lift, bright midrange, stable song form

アニメソング.notes: high-energy vocal pop/rock/electronic anime theme tendency with strong hooks

クラシック音楽.notes: acoustic orchestral/chamber tradition, high dynamics, low beat grid

オペラ.notes: classical vocal focus with large dynamics and acoustic accompaniment

フォーク.notes: acoustic voice/guitar or traditional song, moderate energy

ワールドミュージック.notes: broad macro label; varied acoustic timbres, non-pop rhythmic/harmonic patterns

examples.referenceUrl:
San Francisco's Citay will stop by the WFMU studios for their second appearance, this time on the triumphant heels of their latest release Little Kingdom. Expect multi-layered, orchestrated psychedelia full of delicious hooks. (http://wfmu.org/playlists/shows/26689)

A live set from Mors Ontologica is also featured on this show.
Engineered by Jason Engle, released on  double cdr  by Dan Deacon in 2004. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/3.0

Gary's 1973 opus Red Hash has remained a enduring document of stark, sad acoustic beauty. It's a deeply personal and eccentric record created by someone on the edge of an abyss; in reality Higgins was on the verge of a 3-year sentencing to jail for a marijuana bust. Red Hash, while not distributed properly upon its release, has kept popping up on WFMU playlists over the years (and was also recently documented on the station's blog in detail) and tomorrow (July 27th) Drag City lovingly reissues this elusive album. To celebrate, Gary has resurfaced and joins Brian today with the addition of some Red Hash-era band members in tow. They are: Dave Beaujon: Bass, Graham Higgins: Guitar, Maureen Wells: Cello, Terry Fenton: Keyboard (not in session, just interview) and of course Gary on Vocal/Guitar. Songs: Stable of Spuds, Thicker Than a Smokey. More info at www.dragcity.com. Thank you to Gary & co. Ben, and especially Zach Cowie for his infinite, continual good deeds to me. (http://wfmu.org/playlists/shows/15838)

This previously unrecorded song was featured on WFMU's Free Music Archive sampler vol. 1.

As for Shelley Winters, she was an actress, star of the original Lolita film (we have a poster for this film on the first floor of WFMU -- perhaps it inspired the name?). More on Shelley Winters at Wikipedia

Spain's cathartic, charismatic La Troba Kung Fu is the offspring of the late great band Dusminguet. The buoyant Barcelona-area combo led by accordionist extraordinaire Joan (pronounced like "Juan") Garriga uses the distinctive regional Rumba Catalan style as the "surfboard" for genre-leaping mirth-making on their beautifully packaged debut CD / illustrated chapbook Clavell Morenet (K-Industria Records). This live session was recorded after their triumphant NYC debut at Lincoln Center this past July, opening for Rumba Catalan icon Peret.

(http://wfmu.org/playlists/TP)

Engineered by Diane Farris

High Places bring their amazing brand of pretty, echoey, tropical, tribal, DIY pop up to the WFMU studios for a live set. With layer after layer of sweetness melting together into a tasty fondue for your ears, High Places are a treat not to be missed. Tune it in and turn it up.

http://wfmu.org/playlists/shows/29112

engineered by Trent Wolbe

To celebrate, Gary has resurfaced and joins Brian today with the addition of some Red Hash-era band members in tow. They are: Dave Beaujon: Bass, Graham Higgins: Guitar, Maureen Wells: Cello, Terry Fenton: Keyboard (not in session, just interview) and of course Gary on Vocal/Guitar. Songs: Stable of Spuds, Thicker Than a Smokey. More info at www.dragcity.com. Thank you to Gary & co. Ben, and especially Zach Cowie for his infinite, continual good deeds to me. (http://wfmu.org/playlists/shows/15838)

This previously unrecorded song was featured on WFMU's Free Music Archive sampler vol. 1.

As for Shelley Winters, she was an actress, star of the original Lolita film (we have a poster for this film on the first floor of WFMU -- perhaps it inspired the name?). More on Shelley Winters at Wikipedia

Spain's cathartic, charismatic La Troba Kung Fu is the offspring of the late great band Dusminguet. The buoyant Barcelona-area combo led by accordionist extraordinaire Joan (pronounced like "Juan") Garriga uses the distinctive regional Rumba Catalan style as the "surfboard" for genre-leaping mirth-making on their beautifully packaged debut CD / illustrated chapbook Clavell Morenet (K-Industria Records). This live session was recorded after their triumphant NYC debut at Lincoln Center this past July, opening for Rumba Catalan icon Peret.

(http://wfmu.org/playlists/TP)

High Places bring their amazing brand of pretty, echoey, tropical, tribal, DIY pop up to the WFMU studios for a live set. With layer after layer of sweetness melting together into a tasty fondue for your ears, High Places are a treat not to be missed. Tune it in and turn it up.
